scientific_question: Whether S3 grain reversal persists when graphs are explicitly connected while matching target mean degree.
selection_rule: Only six predeclared S3 grain cells: Sleep/Anesthesia G1, G2, G3.
edge_count_rule: M=round(N*k/2), required M>=N-1; MST backbone plus strongest remaining absolute-correlation edges.
graph_rule: Connectivity-controlled diagnostic graph construction; binary unweighted Louvain graph; no graph repair beyond MST backbone.

reused_intermediates.reason: No persisted hashable correlation matrices were available; existing Phase-1 loader/coarse-graining/window logic was rerun deterministically.

runtime.seed_policy: stable_seed(12345, primary cell_id with _K005, state_index*1000+window_index, repeat)

sleep.interpretation: Substantial G1/G3 reversal persists in connected graphs at both matched degree regimes.

ane.interpretation: Substantial G1/G3 reversal persists in connected graphs at both matched degree regimes.

python_reload_order_sensitivity.meaning: same adjacency edge set; fixed-seed python-louvain Q vectors changed after MAT reload because NetworkX edge insertion order changed

overall_interpretation: Substantial S3 G1/G3 grain reversal persists at both connected matched-degree regimes in both conditions; selected BCT diagnostics preserve the qualitative state direction and reversal.
what_this_weakens: A simple disconnected-graph or isolated-node explanation of the observed S3 grain reversal.
The combined fixed-density -> mean-degree -> fragmentation explanation as a sufficient account of the reversal.
what_remains: Network-size and finite-size modularity effects because G1 has many more nodes than G3.
Exact Q differences due Python graph insertion order and Python-vs-BCT implementation differences.
paper_implication: stronger empirical increment candidate, but still post-primary exploratory and methodological; no SRT/theoretical promotion
next_highest_information_gate: multi-recording or multi-animal replication, if separately authorized; no further graph rule was run here.
